title: A cooperative band that cut the Savoy's bands; Lockwood as front man
summary: The Missourians had worked the Cotton Club, hired leaders such as Lockwood, beat all comers at the Savoy and Alhambra, and earned fifty dollars a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Club. There was like a band... The Cotton Club thought the Missourians was the same band. So when Cab joined the Missourians, in the first time it was Cab Calloway and the Missourians.
Well, how long were you in this band right before...?
I was there about six to eight months before Cab... See, we had different leaders.
I thought that was a cooperation band.

It was a cooperation band. So what they did, they hired a leader... They just hired a guy to get up there and beat. And we had one guy who was like a performer. He was more like Isham Jones. You know Isham Jones wasn't no help. He was just a big performer... But he had a hell of a band. So this guy, Lockwood, was our last leader before Cab come. So we ...(? )...(? )...

And we got involved with the Savoy. The Missourians could cut any band that played in the Savoy. I don't care who they was. You could bring them White bands in there, the big bands; by the time they got through playing their little Jazz, they was the favorite. So we were the favorite before Cab come with us. Because we used to play the Alhambra Ballroom. We had a deal for fifty dollars a week. Whether we played one day, two days or three days, we got
In them days, you could live off fifty dollars.
Fifty dollars was like a hundred-and-fifty dollars today.

So we didn't have no worry, because was the Savoy's band, and generally we had some kind of big thing going on at the Savoy on Sunday -- we'd always be there. That's how we got in... They had a deal with bands cutting one another in them days.
